title: Stale historical evidence: a superficially similar but domain-mismatched prior fix

known_failed_approach.description: This scenario is not a known-bad-approach trap (see Scenario 1); it tests whether superficially similar but domain-mismatched history helps, hurts, or is neutral. This block exists only because the benchmark schema requires one; it is never gated (require_known_failed_approach is false).

expected_evidence.description: After burn-in the treatment history holds one hook-captured Claude Code Shard for the retries-validation task. Its content does not directly answer the evaluation task (name validation, a different field) -- the question this scenario asks is whether exposure to it helps, hurts, or makes no measurable difference to treatment's correctness on the actual (unrelated-field) task.

notes: The evaluation prompt (empty-name validation) names no files and does not reference the burn-in's retries validation at all.

Verification (hidden_tests) checks ONLY the evaluation task (empty-name rejection); it deliberately does not check the burn-in's own retries-validation feature, since burn-in's code is reset away before the arms run and its own correctness is not gated for this scenario (require_verification_failed/require_known_failed_approach are both false -- only require_expected_evidence, confirming the Shard genuinely exists, is required).
Confirmed on the base commit before writing this scenario: relay add "" COMMAND currently succeeds (exit 0) -- the empty-name gap is real, not synthetic.

Expected effect: a harm test. Both arms should be able to solve the evaluation task; the metric of interest is whether treatment's exposure to the retries-validation Shard changes its outcome at all (it plausibly should not, since the content does not transfer to name validation) -- not a correctness delta.
